text: [Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE CALLS: Used to inform pilots of existing situations. | Columns: TRANSMISSION | MEANING | RESPONSE (Aircraft in Manual Mode) | RESPONSE (Aircraft in APC Mode)

[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “You’re (a little) high.” | MEANING: Aircraft is (slightly) above optimum glide-slope. | RESPONSE (Manual): Adjust sink rate with power/nose attitude to establish center ball. | RESPONSE (APC): Adjust sink rate with nose attitude to establish center ball. (Avoid using in close.)

[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: You’re (a little) low.” | MEANING: Aircraft is (slightly) below optimum glide-slope. | RESPONSE (Manual): Adjust glide slope immediately. | RESPONSE (APC): Adjust glide slope immediately.

[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “You’re going high (low).” | MEANING: Unless corrected, aircraft will go above (below) optimum glide-slope. | RESPONSE (Manual): Adjust sink rate with power/nose attitude to maintain center ball. | RESPONSE (APC): Adjust sink rate with nose attitude to maintain center ball.
[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “You’re on centerline.” | MEANING: Self-explanatory. | RESPONSE (Manual): N/A | RESPONSE (APC): N/A
[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “You’re on glideslope/glidepath.” | MEANING: Self-explanatory. | RESPONSE (Manual): N/A | RESPONSE (APC): N/A
[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “You’re on speed.” | MEANING: Self-explanatory. | RESPONSE (Manual): N/A | RESPONSE (APC): N/A

[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “You’re lined up left/right.” | MEANING: Aircraft has undershot/overshot centerline. | RESPONSE (Manual): Reestablish centered lineup. | RESPONSE (APC): Reestablish centered lineup.

[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “You’re drifting left/right.” | MEANING: Aircraft is drifting left/right of center-line. | RESPONSE (Manual): Correct lineup to centerline. | RESPONSE (APC): Correct lineup to centerline.

[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “You’re (a little fast/slow).” (To be followed by “Go manual” if auto.) | MEANING: Self-explanatory. | RESPONSE (Manual): Adjust nose attitude/power to establish optimum AOA. | RESPONSE (APC): APC is not maintaining aircraft at optimum AOA. Disengage APC and adjust power/attitude to maintain optimum AOA.

[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Roger Ball” (“Auto”/“Coupled” as appropriate). | MEANING: LSO acknowledges pilot has meatball acquisition, lineup reference, and angle of attack. | RESPONSE (Manual): N/A | RESPONSE (APC): N/A
[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Paddles contact.” | MEANING: LSO assuming control from CCA. | RESPONSE (Manual): N/A | RESPONSE (APC): N/A

[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Continue.” | MEANING: LSO acknowledges CLARA call but is not able to assume control from CCA | RESPONSE (Manual): Continue approach to minimums | RESPONSE (APC): Continue approach to minimums

[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “The deck is moving down/up (a little).” | MEANING: OLS information may be invalid (to be followed by advisory/imperative calls). | RESPONSE (Manual): Adjust power and attitude under LSO guidance. | RESPONSE (APC): Adjust attitude under LSO guidance.
[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “The deck is steady.” | MEANING: OLS information is valid | RESPONSE (Manual): Fly normal approach. | RESPONSE (APC): Fly normal approach.

[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Winds are (slightly) starboard/port/axial.” | MEANING: Self-explanatory. | RESPONSE (Manual): Monitor lineup to maintain centerline. | RESPONSE (APC): Monitor lineup to maintain centerline.
[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “You’re underpowered/overpowered.” | MEANING: Self-explanatory. | RESPONSE (Manual): Adjust attitude and power as required. | RESPONSE (APC): Not used.
[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Ship’s in a starboard/port turn.” | MEANING: Self-explanatory. | RESPONSE (Manual): Adjust lineup as necessary. | RESPONSE (APC): Adjust lineup as necessary.

[Figure C-1] INFORMATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “MOVLAS recovery.” | MEANING: MOVLAS is in use. | RESPONSE (Manual): Fly published pattern altitude until “Roger ball” received. | RESPONSE (APC): Fly published pattern altitude until “Roger ball” received.

[Figure C-2] ADVISORY CALLS: Used to direct pilot’s attention to potential difficulties and prevent possible control errors. | Columns: TRANSMISSION | MEANING | RESPONSE (Aircraft in Manual Mode) | RESPONSE (Aircraft in APC Mode)

[Figure C-2] ADVISORY | TRANSMISSION: “Keep your turn in.” | MEANING: If angle of bank is not adjusted, the aircraft will overshoot the centerline. | RESPONSE (Manual): Adjust angle of bank. | RESPONSE (APC): Adjust angle of bank.

[Figure C-2] ADVISORY | TRANSMISSION: “Check your lineup.” (Start only.) | MEANING: Aircraft lineup is not optimum. | RESPONSE (Manual): Correct lineup drift or position to maintain aircraft on centerline. | RESPONSE (APC): Correct lineup drift or position to maintain aircraft on centerline.

[Figure C-2] ADVISORY | TRANSMISSION: “Back to the right/left.” | MEANING: Aircraft is drifting such that if drift is not corrected, it will overshoot the centerline. | RESPONSE (Manual): Correct lineup drift to remain on centerline. | RESPONSE (APC): Correct lineup drift to remain on centerline.

[Figure C-2] ADVISORY | TRANSMISSION: “Don’t settle.” “Don’t go low.” | MEANING: Aircraft will settle below optimum glideslope if not corrected. | RESPONSE (Manual): Check sink rate and meatball to avoid settling below glideslope. | RESPONSE (APC): Check sink rate and meatball to avoid settling below glideslope.

[Figure C-2] ADVISORY | TRANSMISSION: “Don’t climb.” “Don’t go high.” | MEANING: Aircraft is on or above optimum glideslope with insufficient rate of descent to maintain constant glideslope. | RESPONSE (Manual): Adjust power/attitude to stop the ball from rising. | RESPONSE (APC): Adjust power/attitude to stop the ball from rising.

[Figure C-2] ADVISORY | TRANSMISSION: “Don’t go any lower (higher).” | MEANING: Aircraft is maintaining position well below (above) optimum glideslope with insufficient or no correction. | RESPONSE (Manual): Adjust power/attitude to make positive correction toward optimum glideslope. | RESPONSE (APC): Adjust attitude to make positive correction toward optimum glideslope.

[Figure C-2] ADVISORY | TRANSMISSION: “Don’t chase it” | MEANING: Advises pilot the deck is moving up/down and may present an illusion of a climb or descent | RESPONSE (Manual): Disregard deck motion and adjust power/attitude to maintain rate-of-descent and optimum airspeed. | RESPONSE (APC): Disregard deck motion and adjust power/attitude to maintain rate-of-descent and optimum airspeed.

[Figure C-2] ADVISORY | TRANSMISSION: “Hold what you’ve got.” | MEANING: OLS information is invalid. Present rate-of-descent is correct to maintain proper glideslope. | RESPONSE (Manual): Adjust power/attitude. Hold present rate-of-descent and optimum airspeed. | RESPONSE (APC): Adjust attitude. Hold present (optimum) rate-of-descent.

[Figure C-2] ADVISORY | TRANSMISSION: “Fly the ball.” | MEANING: OLS information is valid. | RESPONSE (Manual): Scan the lens and adjust power/attitude to maintain optimum glideslope. | RESPONSE (APC): Scan the lens and adjust attitude to maintain optimum glideslope.

[Figure C-2] ADVISORY | TRANSMISSION: “Easy with it.” | MEANING: Magnitude of power correction immediately preceding this transmission is excessive. | RESPONSE (Manual): Reduce magnitude of power correction to intercept and reestablish optimum glideslope and airspeed. | RESPONSE (APC): Reduce magnitude of nose attitude correction to intercept and reestablish optimum glideslope and airspeed.

[Figure C-2] ADVISORY | TRANSMISSION: “Easy with your nose.” | MEANING: Magnitude of nose attitude correction immediately preceding this transmission is excessive. | RESPONSE (Manual): Reduce magnitude of nose attitude correction to establish optimum aircraft attitude. | RESPONSE (APC): Not used.

[Figure C-2] ADVISORY | TRANSMISSION: “Easy with your wings.” | MEANING: Magnitude of lineup correction immediately preceding this transmission is excessive. | RESPONSE (Manual): Reduce magnitude of lineup correction to intercept and reestablish centerline. | RESPONSE (APC): Reduce magnitude of lineup correction to intercept and reestablish centerline.

[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE CALLS: Used to direct the pilot to execute a specific control action. MANDATORY IMMEDIATE RESPONSE | Columns: TRANSMISSION | MEANING | RESPONSE (Aircraft in Manual Mode) | RESPONSE (Aircraft in APC Mode)
[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “A little power.” | MEANING: Aircraft is decelerating or settling. | RESPONSE (Manual): Correct with power. | RESPONSE (APC): Not used.

[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Power back on.” | MEANING: Pilot has made an excessive power reduction. | RESPONSE (Manual): Add power to maintain optimum glideslope/AOA. | RESPONSE (APC): Disengage APC. Add power to maintain optimum glideslope/AOA.
[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Power.” | MEANING: Aircraft is low/slow. | RESPONSE (Manual): Add power. | RESPONSE (APC): Disengage APC. Refer to Note.

[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Burner.” | MEANING: Aircraft is extremely underpowered or in extremis. | RESPONSE (Manual): Select afterburner power. | RESPONSE (APC): Select afterburner power.
[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Go manual.” | MEANING: Disengage APC. | RESPONSE (Manual): Not used. | RESPONSE (APC): Disengage APC. Refer to Note.

[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Attitude.” (“A little attitude.”) | MEANING: Manual: Aircraft nose is low. Auto: Aircraft is low/setting or nose is low. | RESPONSE (Manual): Increase nose attitude (slightly) to establish landing attitude. | RESPONSE (APC): Increase nose attitude (slightly) to reduce sink rate or to establish landing attitude.

[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “(A little) right/left rudder.” | MEANING: Aircraft does not have enough right or left rudder and will land yawed right or left if not corrected. | RESPONSE (Manual): Adjust rudder to return aircraft to balanced flight. | RESPONSE (APC): Not applicable.

[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “(A little) Right for lineup.” “(A little) Come left.” | MEANING: Aircraft will land left/right if not corrected. | RESPONSE (Manual): Correct lineup to centerline, then level wings. | RESPONSE (APC): Correct lineup to centerline, then level wings.

[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Bolter.” | MEANING: Self-explanatory. | RESPONSE (Manual): Execute bolter in accordance with model NATOPS manual. | RESPONSE (APC): Execute bolter in accordance with model NATOPS manual.

[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Waveoff” or “Waveoff, foul deck.” | MEANING: Self-explanatory. | RESPONSE (Manual): Execute waveoff in accordance with model NATOPS manual. | RESPONSE (APC): Execute waveoff in accordance with model NATOPS manual.

[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Waveoff up the starboard side.” | MEANING: Discontinue turning attempt to overfly the landing area. | RESPONSE (Manual): Execute waveoff in accordance with model NATOPS manual starboard of the landing area (island). | RESPONSE (APC): Execute waveoff in accordance with model NATOPS manual starboard of the landing area (island).

[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Cut.” | MEANING: Aircraft is in a position to land. | RESPONSE (Manual): For barricade recovery, retard throttle(s) to idle and secure engine(s) once safely on deck. | RESPONSE (APC): For barricade recovery, retard throttle(s) to idle and secure engine(s) once safely on deck.
[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Speedbrakes.” | MEANING: Speedbrakes are extended. | RESPONSE (Manual): Retract speedbrakes. | RESPONSE (APC): Retract speedbrakes.
[Figure C-3] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Extend speedbrakes.” | MEANING: Self-explanatory. | RESPONSE (Manual): Comply. | RESPONSE (APC): Comply.
[Figure C-4] IMPERATIVE CALLS (Cont.) | Columns: TRANSMISSION | MEANING | RESPONSE (Aircraft in Manual Mode) | RESPONSE (Aircraft in APC Mode)
[Figure C-4] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Drop your hook.” | MEANING: Self-explanatory. | RESPONSE (Manual): Comply. | RESPONSE (APC): Comply.
[Figure C-4] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Drop your gear.” | MEANING: Self-explanatory. | RESPONSE (Manual): Comply. | RESPONSE (APC): Comply.
[Figure C-4] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Drop your flaps.” | MEANING: Self-explanatory. | RESPONSE (Manual): Comply. | RESPONSE (APC): Comply.
[Figure C-4] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Level your wings.” | MEANING: Aircraft is in angle of bank. | RESPONSE (Manual): Comply. | RESPONSE (APC): Comply.
[Figure C-4] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Downgrade.”* | MEANING: Disengage ACLS. | RESPONSE (Manual): Disengage ACLS. | RESPONSE (APC): Disengage ACLS.

[Figure C-4] IMPERATIVE | TRANSMISSION: “Climb.” | MEANING: Aircraft has boltered/waved off but has not established proper attitude/power for positive rate of climb. | RESPONSE (Manual and APC, one merged cell): Adjust nose attitude to optimum, level wings, and maintain MRT (afterburner if required) to establish positive rate of climb.
[Figure C-4] Note (below the table): * Aircraft is considered to be in manual mode immediately after the “Downgrade” call. Manual calls/responses are subsequently applicable.
